concept: A streak story told as a countdown that stops. The hero puts the run in muted grey (13 wins in a row. Two titles.) and the full stop in bright white (Then Anders Antonsen.) so the turn lands before any score. Slide 2 gives the streak one giant 13, slide 3 answers why it ended with one giant 6-3, the head-to-head that now tilts further to Antonsen, and slide 4 does the same for the doubles with the 19-21 that closed out Satwik-Chirag. The last slide moves the story forward to Hangzhou, where both men meet again in the top-eight field. Indian-sport orange, type and numbers only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
13 wins in a row. Two titles. Then Anders Antonsen.

Lakshya Sen reached the Hong Kong Open semi-finals on a 13-match winning streak built on back-to-back titles at the Hylo Open and the Kumamoto Masters. That run equalled Kidambi Srikanth's 13 straight wins from 2017.

Antonsen ended it on Saturday. The Danish world No. 3 won 21-13, 21-13 in 42 minutes (as reported by RevSportz) and now leads their head-to-head 6-3. Lakshya has never beaten him in Asia.

Earlier in the day Satwik-Chirag lost 18-21, 19-21 to Malaysia's Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun after leading 7-3 in the second game.

A rematch could come soon. Lakshya and Antonsen are both in the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from December 9 to 13.
